result.title: Where Demand Meets Supply: Spatial Elastic Consensus for Low-Bandwidth Collaborative Perception
result.summary: Occlusions and limited sensor range make ego-only 3D perception insufficient for safe driving. Collaborative perception addresses this by enabling connected vehicles to share complementary observations, yet it remains constrained by tight vehicular communication budgets. While spatial selection is more flexible than fixed-rate feature compression, existing selectors remain largely sender-driven and waste scarce bandwidth on ego-visible targets. Furthermore, applying convolutions after masking spreads isolated tokens into their neighborhoods, silently violating low-bandwidth constraints. To address this, we propose Spatial Elastic Consensus (SEC), a bandwidth-adaptive framework centered on bilateral demand-supply consensus. Instead of unilateral token selection, the ego vehicle formulates a content-aware demand prior while each collaborator evaluates its local supply. This single-round consensus allocates the token budget to critical ego-missed evidence rather than ego-visible redundancy, without transmitting dense maps. To guarantee exact budget compliance, an anti-dilation refine-before-mask pipeline refines features prior to discrete token selection, preventing receptive-field leakage. A lightweight deformable sampler then aggregates these sparse messages with learned local offsets, compensating for the spatial context lost to token selection and mitigating inter-agent pose drift. Evaluated at a stringent 64KiB budget, SEC consistently achieves the best AP@0.7 on the simulated OPV2V and V2XSet datasets and the real-world DAIR-V2X dataset. These results demonstrate that combining bilateral consensus with budget-exact transmission is key to efficient low-bandwidth collaborative perception.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Spatial Elastic Consensus 框架：自车生成内容感知的需求先验、协作者评估本地供给，单轮共识把有限带宽分配给自车被遮挡而缺失的证据，并以 refine-before-mask 与可变形采样器保证预算严格合规，在 64KiB 下提升协同 3D 检测精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「需求—供给」双边稀疏证据选择、抑制自车已见冗余及预算精确约束，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、LOOK 的成本控制与信息价值判断提供问题表述参考；但对象是 3D 协同检测而非 VLM 推理，迁移可行性需核查。
